correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=1 the sample space is exactly C(2n,n) equally weighted tied-down +/-1 bridges; positive-time returns include the last endpoint and one-sided maximum includes time zero. Reflection at h+1 gives B_h(z)=B(z)(1-q(z)^(h+1)); marking completed first-return excursions gives derivative B_h^2-B_h. Summing level exceedances and rationalizing yields mixed GF 3/(4s^3)-1/s^2+1/(4s), hence E(K_n M_n)=3n/2+1-R_n. Second derivatives and tail-square binomial identities give every stated marginal and variance. The exact positive ratio [R_(n+1)^2/(3n+4)]/[R_n^2/(3n+1)]=1+n/((2n+1)^2(3n+4)) with equality at n=1 proves strictly negative covariance for all n>=2. Stirling then proves the covariance/correlation limits. Independent exact DP through n=34, complete stepping-word enumeration through n=9 and 199 exact ratio instances (577 checks total) agree; finite tests merely corroborate the universal proof. A separate symbolic simplification checked the mixed GF identity.
residual_risks: The binary bridge model and the endpoint counting convention are essential; claims do not include absolute maxima, biased walks, or negative association for all functions.
No executable proof assistant certification or external expert attestation is present; analytic steps were manually reconstructed.

Fresh searches of published findings plus full primary examination of the most relevant lattice excursion/maximum sources identified the separate marginal and ranked-height laws but not the precise mixed cross moment. residual_risks: Classical reflection and excursion renewal techniques could already encode E[K_n M_n] in an older two-parameter ballot path enumeration without naming the covariance explicitly.

Published unconditioned max-return generating function, October 18, 2026
value.rationale: The two observables are naturally central to conditioned random walks: K_n counts first-return excursions (discrete origin local time), whereas M_n records a spatial extreme. Even complete individual marginals leave their dependence undetermined. A closed formula for every length, strict n>=2 anticorrelation, linear covariance decay with coefficient (3-pi)/2 and nonvanishing limiting Pearson correlation (3-pi)/(4-pi) form a useful exact discrete benchmark for bridge renewal/excursion methods and Brownian limits. This is a motivated joint-invariant result rather than an arbitrary small parameter slice or renaming of a known area/energy covariance.
residual_risks: Known reflection and renewal methods make the derivation relatively short and may limit novelty if stronger equivalent joint enumerators are subsequently located.
The continuum limiting correlation can be implicit in older Brownian joint-law literature, so primary new utility is the exact finite-size bridge identity and all-n sign rule.

limitations: Strict covariance sign only for n>=2, equality at n=1; correlation defined where variances are positive.
Global maximum is one-sided and includes the initial origin; return count includes the final time 2n.
One may not replace the maximum with integrated height, absolute height, or longest excursion duration.
Best-of-knowledge originality is qualified by possible broader, implicit classic enumerations.
Scientific review does not imply GitHub publication, a Lean proof or expert attestation.
